Descriptives and regression

Source: vignettes/articles/descriptives-models.Rmd
descriptives-models.Rmd

Prepare one survey design

Declare the cohort in nis_design() and keep the columns needed by the summary and model.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50") |>
  nis_outcomes()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpiLRxxQ/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpiLRxxQ/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, LOS, in_hospital_death, heart_failure),
  annualize = TRUE
)
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.

The design contains adult cohort rows. For hospital-years with no cohort rows, nis_design() adds placeholder rows so those hospital-years remain represented in the design’s variance structure. This placeholder method is experimental; review the design construction and its suitability for your analysis.

Estimate weighted summaries

srvyr adds tidy verbs to survey designs. The total below is an annualized weighted discharge estimate; the mean and its standard error use the survey design.

srvyr::summarise(
  design,
  discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
  mean_age = srvyr::survey_mean(AGE),
  death_proportion = srvyr::survey_mean(in_hospital_death, na.rm = TRUE)
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   discharges discharges_se mean_age mean_age_se death_proportion
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1       114.          2.83     59.6       0.597           0.0201
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: death_proportion_se <dbl>

All values come from invented rows and illustrate output shape only.

Fit a survey-weighted model

survey::svyglm() fits generalized linear models using the design.

fit <- survey::svyglm(
  in_hospital_death ~ heart_failure + AGE + FEMALE + factor(YEAR),
  design = design,
  family = quasibinomial()
)
term <- "heart_failureTRUE"
interval <- exp(confint(fit, parm = term))
data.frame(
  model_n = nrow(stats::model.frame(fit)),
  odds_ratio = exp(coef(fit)[[term]]),
  lower = interval[1L],
  upper = interval[2L]
)
#>   model_n odds_ratio      lower   upper
#> 1     192  0.4178614 0.01056816 16.5221

The odds ratio compares adult discharges with and without a recorded heart failure diagnosis at the same age, sex, and year in this model. The model frame counts discharges with complete values for this formula. The interval uses design-based standard errors and the model’s residual degrees of freedom. The results illustrate an adjusted association in invented data.

Contrast two mean lengths of stay

With a single binary predictor, the Gaussian survey model coefficient is the difference in weighted mean LOS, in days. It subtracts the mean among discharges without a heart failure code from the mean among discharges with one. The fit gives the design-based standard error of the difference.

los_difference <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ heart_failure, design = design)
nrow(stats::model.frame(los_difference))
#> [1] 192
summary(los_difference)$coefficients[term, ]
#>   Estimate Std. Error    t value   Pr(>|t|) 
#>  0.2826923  0.4126637  0.6850428  0.5025514
confint(los_difference, parm = term)
#>                       2.5 %   97.5 %
#> heart_failureTRUE -0.587952 1.153337

Report the complete-case discharge count for each model. See Survey design and weighting for an example that changes the target of the mean contrast through reweighting.

Tables with gtsummary

The examples below use gtsummary 2.6.1 or later.

Pass the result of nis_design() directly to gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(). The design supplies cohort discharges for unweighted sample sizes, missing counts, and category counts. Hospital placeholders contribute to the variance structure only. This table uses a survey t-test for mean age and the design-adjusted chi-squared test for sex. The header shows unweighted sample sizes, alongside weighted summaries in the table body.

The default continuous summary uses a weighted median and quartiles. On a large cohort, computing those quantiles for each group can dominate table runtime. Use include to select the variables the table needs. When a weighted mean answers the scientific question, request one explicitly with statistic = AGE ~ "{mean} ({mean.std.error})".

gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = heart_failure,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE),
  label = FEMALE ~ "Female",
  statistic = AGE ~ "{mean} ({mean.std.error})",
  missing_stat = "{N_miss_unweighted}"
) |>
  gtsummary::add_p(test = list(AGE ~ "svy.t.test", FEMALE ~ "svy.chisq.test")) |>
  gtsummary::add_overall() |>
  gtsummary::modify_header(gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}** (unweighted N = {n_unweighted})")
Characteristic TRUE (unweighted N = 108)1 Overall (unweighted N = 192)1 FALSE (unweighted N = 84)1 p-value2
Age, years 58 (1) 60 (1) 62 (1) 0.035
Female 31 (50%) 57 (50%) 26 (50%) >0.9
1 Mean (SE); n (%)
2 Design-based t-test; Pearson’s X^2: Rao & Scott adjustment

Use tbl_regression() to format your fitted models and tbl_uvregression() to fit and format a separate survey model for each predictor. The logistic table reports odds ratios and the linear tables report differences in mean length of stay.

For Parquet inputs, start with nis_open() and then use nis_design() to build the in-memory cohort design used here. Passing a DuckDB-backed survey DBIsvydesign directly to tbl_svysummary() fails with gtsummary 2.6.1. Review unweighted cell counts and apply disclosure rules before sharing.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Use survey/srvyr methods on the survey design, not ordinary row-level summaries when reporting design-based uncertainty.
  • A weighted estimate does not validate the cohort definition, model, or causal interpretation.
  • Apply disclosure review separately; weighted summaries alone do not show whether counts are safe to report.

See Survey design and weighting, nis_design(), and Disclosure and suppression.

Whole-sample estimation on a laptop

Use nis_survey() to estimate means, totals, or regression coefficients when discharge rows would take too much memory. It uses a nested Taylor design with hospital-year PSUs and year-specific strata. DuckDB scans the Parquet data and sends weighted PSU sums to R. Use dplyr::filter() on the design to estimate a domain. subset(whole, AGE >= 65) is the survey-style alternative. Filtering the query before constructing the design changes the sample.

whole <- nis_survey(nis)
older <- dplyr::filter(whole, AGE >= 65)
survey::svyby(~LOS, ~YEAR, older, survey::svymean)
#>      YEAR      LOS        se
#> 2019 2019 4.577143 0.4142243
#> 2020 2020 4.577143 0.4142243
fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ AGE + factor(YEAR), older)
broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   term             estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>               <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)        15.3      3.08        4.96 0.000143    8.73    21.8   
#> 2 AGE                -0.138    0.0373     -3.70 0.00196    -0.217   -0.0588
#> 3 factor(YEAR)2020    0        0.586       0    1          -1.24     1.24

For a nis_survey() fit, gtsummary::tbl_regression() reports the unweighted number of complete discharges as N. For a nis_design() fit, N comes from the analysis weights.

Use nis_design() for row-level cohort analysis, including quantiles, chi-square tests, gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(), and IPTW. Use the disclosure workflow before sharing results.
